key_insight: Step-Decomposed Influence (SDI) breaks a single TracIn score into a length-τ vector of per-iteration influence, revealing exactly which loop iteration(s) a training example affects during latent reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing influence estimators collapse all recurrent iterations into one scalar, hiding when during a shared-block (looped) transform the training data matter; SDI makes influence step-resolved and interpretable.
method: Decompose TracIn by evaluating gradient contributions at each of the τ recurrent iterations of the shared transformer block to produce a per-step influence vector.
Aggregate and normalize these per-step gradient inner products to form a length-τ influence trace (SDI) that sums to the original TracIn score.
Use checkpoints / efficient approximations to compute SDI in practice and provide visual summaries (e.g., heatmaps, cumulative vs stepwise plots) for analysis.
impact: SDI lets practitioners localize dataset influence in time across recurrent inference, enabling finer-grained debugging, targeted data interventions (pruning/augmentation/label fixes), and better understanding of latent reasoning dynamics.
visual_elements: Schematic of a looped transformer: one shared block unrolled over τ iterations with per-step influence scores annotated on each pass
Heatmap: training examples (rows) × loop steps (columns) showing magnitude and sign of SDI to identify which examples matter at which steps
Bar / line plots comparing aggregated (scalar) TracIn vs. cumulative and per-step SDI for representative examples
Flowchart showing SDI computation: checkpoint gradient extraction → per-step inner products → normalization → visualization
paper_title: Step-resolved data attribution for looped transformers
paper_authors: Georgios Kaissis, David Mildenberger, Juan Felipe Gomez, Martin J. Menten, Eleni Triantafillou
